text: The Fallout roleplaying game's core rulebook says the government promised a program to save the whole population, but only 122 Vaults were ever commissioned, enough for less than 0.1% of the population.

sources.title: Fallout: The Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook
sources.locator: Core Rulebook p. 250 (Modiphius)
sources.quote: Although the government promised a program to save the entire populace, only 122 such shelters were even commissioned, an order that could support less than 0.1% of the population.

label: as-reported

ruling.why: No tier 1 source known to contradict it: the games and show give no exact total, only 'well over 100' planned (Fallout 4 newscaster, VT-0002).

text: The Fallout roleplaying game's core rulebook calls the Vault program Project Safehouse and says it was never meant to save the US population in a nuclear catastrophe.

sources.title: Fallout: The Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook
sources.locator: Core Rulebook p. 251 (Modiphius)
sources.quote: Project Safehouse was never intended to save the U.S. population in the event of a nuclear catastrophe.

label: as-reported

ruling.why: No tier 1 source known to contradict it; Fallout 2's President Richardson calls the Vaults a social experiment on a grand scale (VT-0053). The name Project Safehouse was not seen in a tier 1 source in this batch.

text: The rulebook says certain hands in government subverted Project Safehouse to preserve 'approved' portions of society: some 17 Vaults were commissioned and built to preserve those approved by a shadow government.

sources.title: Fallout: The Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook
sources.locator: Core Rulebook p. 251 (Modiphius)
sources.quote: Instead, certain hands in government subverted it to preserve certain...approved... portions of society. Some 17 of the vaults were commissioned and built with that in mind, created to preserve those approved by the shadow government.

label: as-reported

ruling.why: No tier 1 source known to contradict it. Fallout 3's Citadel terminal gives the same number of control Vaults, 17 (VT-0061), but does not say whom they were for.

text: The rulebook says the other 105 Vaults were built as experiments: they protected their people from the bombs, but life afterwards was engineered for stress and challenge.

sources.title: Fallout: The Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook
sources.locator: Core Rulebook p. 250 (Modiphius)
sources.quote: The other 105 vaults were built as experiments. They would house humans, protecting them from the bombs well enough, but life afterward was engineered for stress and challenge.

label: as-reported

ruling.why: No tier 1 source known to contradict it; it fits Fallout 2's account of the Vaults as experiments (VT-0053) and the 17 control Vaults of Fallout 3 (VT-0061).

text: The rulebook reports a rumour that once those 17 Vaults were finished, elements of government hastened or even caused the Great War so their vision of a changed society could come about, and that a few suspect the plan lives on through the Enclave; it says nobody can prove or disprove it.

sources.title: Fallout: The Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook
sources.locator: Core Rulebook p. 251 (Modiphius)
sources.quote: Some say, once they were completed, elements of government hastened or even caused the Great War, so their vision for a changed society could come to fruition. Nobody can prove or disprove that now, though a few suspect those plans live on through the machinations of The Enclave.

label: as-reported

ruling.why: Framed by the source itself as rumour. Who started the Great War is left open in the games; the TV series (tier 1) shows Vault-Tec executives planning around the war, a different account, so whether this fits is unclear.

text: The rulebook says that even with a full list of publicly known Vaults, it is impossible to know how many more were built in secret by the government, private enterprise or Vault-Tec itself.

sources.title: Fallout: The Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook
sources.locator: Core Rulebook p. 252 (Modiphius)
sources.quote: Even with access to a full accounting of publicly known Vaults, it’s impossible to know how many others were secretly constructed by the government, private enterprise, or Vault-Tec itself.

label: as-reported

ruling.why: No tier 1 source known to contradict it; Fallout 76 has a Vault built in secret (Vault 79, VT-0088).

text: The rulebook says a demonstration Vault was opened to the public in Los Angeles near Vault-Tec's headquarters, and public enthusiasm for it helped fund the junk bond drive that paid for the rest of Vault construction.

sources.title: Fallout: The Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook
sources.locator: Core Rulebook p. 250 (Modiphius)
sources.quote: After a demo Vault was opened to the public in Los Angeles, near the Vault-Tec headquarters, public enthusiasm helped fund the junk bond drive that funded the rest of construction.

label: as-reported

ruling.why: No tier 1 source known to contradict it; Fallout (1997) has a former demonstration Vault under the Cathedral (VT-0067), and Chris Taylor placed it near Vault-Tec's headquarters (VT-0130).
